subproblem.title: Dilation averaging estimate on the boundary annulus of the unit ball
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let F : ℝⁿ → ℝ be measurable with F ≥ 0 and F integrable on B := B̆_1(0) (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), and let 0 < s ≤ 1/2. Put A_s := B ∖ B̆_{1−s}(0). Then ∫_{A_s} (∫_{1/2}^1 F(tx) dt) dx ≤ 2^{n+1} s ∫_B F, with Bochner integrals and an interval integral inside.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → ℝ) (s : ℝ), Measurable F → (∀ y, 0 ≤ F y) → IntegrableOn F (ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) → 0 < s → s ≤ 1 / 2 → ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1 \ ball (0 : Euclid n) (1 - s), (∫ t in (1 / 2 : ℝ)..1, F (t • x)) ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) * s * ∫ y in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, F y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3(iv) (dilation estimate). It is carried out with lower Lebesgue integrals, which removes all integrability side conditions.

1. (Reduction to lintegrals.) Let I(x) := ∫_{1/2}^1 F(tx) dt.
- If I is not integrable on A_s, the left side is 0 (integral_undef) and the right side is ≥ 0, so we are done.
- Otherwise, I ≥ 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg) and F ≥ 0 is integrable on B. So ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal converts both sides, and ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff reduces the claim to
∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal(I(x)) dx ≤ ofReal(2^{n+1}s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F.
- For each x, ofReal(I(x)) ≤ ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ofReal(F(tx)) dt. This is an equality by ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal if t ↦ F(tx) is integrable on (1/2,1] (after intervalIntegral.integral_of_le); otherwise I(x) = 0.
It therefore suffices to prove
(*) ∫⁻_{A_s} ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ofReal F(tx) dt dx ≤ ofReal(2^{n+1}s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F.

2. (Tonelli.) The map (x, t) ↦ ofReal F(t•x) is measurable, so lintegral_lintegral_swap exchanges the order of integration: the left side of (*) equals ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal F(tx) dx dt.

3. (Change of variables.) Let T := {(t, y) : t(1 − s) ≤ ‖y‖ < t}, a measurable set (measurableSet_le, measurableSet_lt), and H(t, y) := 1_T(t, y)·ofReal F(y).
- For t > 0 we have x ∈ A_s ⟺ (t, tx) ∈ T, because ‖tx‖ = t‖x‖. So 1_{A_s}(x)·ofReal F(tx) = H(t, tx).
- The image of Lebesgue measure under x ↦ t•x is |t^{−n}|·Lⁿ (Measure.map_addHaar_smul, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
- By lintegral_indicator, lintegral_map and lintegral_smul_measure: ∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal F(tx) dx = |t^{−n}| ∫⁻ H(t, y) dy ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻ H(t, y) dy for t ∈ (1/2, 1].

4. (Tonelli again.) Hence ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal F(tx) dx dt ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ∫⁻ H(t, y) dy dt = 2ⁿ ∫⁻_y ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} H(t, y) dt dy (lintegral_const_mul', lintegral_lintegral_swap).

5. (Length estimate.) Fix y.
- If ‖y‖ ≥ 1, then for t ∈ (1/2, 1] we cannot have ‖y‖ < t, so the inner integral is 0.
- If ‖y‖ < 1, then (t, y) ∈ T implies t ∈ (‖y‖, ‖y‖/(1 − s)], using 1 − s > 0. So
∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} H(t, y) dt ≤ ofReal F(y)·Leb(Ioc ‖y‖ (‖y‖/(1 − s))) = ofReal F(y)·ofReal(‖y‖s/(1 − s)) ≤ ofReal F(y)·ofReal(2s) (lintegral_indicator_const, Real.volume_Ioc), because ‖y‖ < 1 and 1 − s ≥ 1/2.
In both cases ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} H(t, y) dt ≤ 1_B(y)·ofReal(2s)·ofReal F(y).

6. Combining steps 2–5: the left side of (*) is ≤ 2ⁿ·ofReal(2s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F = ofReal(2^{n+1}s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F (lintegral_indicator, ENNReal.ofReal_mul). This is (*), and step 1 finishes the proof. ∎

Validation note (not part of the argument): a kernel-checked Lean proof of this exact frozen statement was compiled during decomposition review as Submission.dorag_ha_rb_dilation_average in /tmp/rellich-validate/Full/Full.lean (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). That scratch file may not persist.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to the lintegral inequality ∫⁻_{A_s}∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ofReal F(tx) ≤ ofReal(2^{n+1}s)∫⁻_B ofReal F; the non-integrable case is trivial.
Change of variables y = tx (Measure.map_addHaar_smul): ∫_{A_s} F(tx) dx = t^{−n}∫ 1_{tA_s}F ≤ 2ⁿ∫ 1_{tA_s}F, with tA_s = {t(1 − s) ≤ ‖y‖ < t} ⊆ B.
Tonelli again; for ‖y‖ < 1 the admissible t lie in (‖y‖, ‖y‖/(1 − s)], of length ≤ 2s, and for ‖y‖ ≥ 1 there are none.

audit.reason: The lintegral reduction correctly handles nonintegrable Bochner integrands. Tonelli, the Jacobian bound t⁻ⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ, and the admissible-parameter length bound 2s give exactly 2^(n+1)s under the stated hypotheses.
